claims.text: Fixed EAM reference potentials cannot adequately represent the many atomic configurations of an ab initio multicomponent-alloy liquid.
An actively trained machine-learning potential will capture the diverse configurations of an ab initio high-entropy-alloy liquid better than a fixed EAM potential.
The machine-learning reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Actively learned moment-tensor potentials can be parameterized with ab initio data for finite-temperature refractory multicomponent alloys.
The proposed reference potential can be actively trained specifically on ab initio high-temperature liquid configurations.
Deep neural-network potentials can describe both solid and liquid structures in a high-entropy material.
The ML framework will sample local liquid arrangements and capture structural heterogeneities ignored by fixed EAM potentials.
Training on diverse liquid configurations will more accurately map the complex ab initio liquid energy landscape.
Improved representation of the liquid energy landscape will lower cumulative free-energy errors during thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method is applicable at approximately 3000–3500 K for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The relevant high melting temperatures are typically above 1850 degrees Celsius.
The method applies to refractory multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near melting.
Free-energy integration errors may be reduced by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Incomplete sampling of rare liquid configurations may degrade the quality and transferability of the ML reference.
A controlled comparison of ML and EAM references under identical conditions can test the proposed reduction in path mismatch and free-energy error.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in path mismatch or improved convergence would falsify the hypothesis.
